title: Compare like reliability with like
statement: Compare a reliability figure only with the same kind of reliability measured under like conditions, because one test's marginal, test-retest and sub-score reliabilities can differ markedly.
example: One reference test reported 0.96 marginal reliability on its calibrated pool, 0.82–0.89 test-retest and 0.87–0.88 for its sub-scores.
detail: An adversarial review set a proxy test's simulated reliability of 0.931 against the reference test's operational 0.96. The package's reply cited the reference test's technical report for 2024–25: the 0.96 is marginal reliability of the operational adaptive test on a fully calibrated pool, its test-retest reliability across terms is 0.82–0.89, and its sub-scores average 0.87–0.88. It called holding a pre-calibration simulation to the operational-pool figure a category error, and its simulation evidence names 0.96 after calibration, not before, as the comparison to hold it to.
against: The review still read the result as a near miss: "0.931 meets the self-set ≥0.93 target but sits below MAP's 0.96 operational bar, on provisional b-values" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md`, line 57). The published figures were read from the package's citation of the report's tables, which gives no DOI or URL, and were not checked against the report itself.

evidence.quote: | Marginal reliability (Table 7.7) | 0.96 | Operational CAT, fully calibrated pool, N ≈ 800K–980K per grade/term |
| Test-retest reliability (Table 7.10) | 0.82–0.89 | Same instrument, real students, across terms — with NWEA's own caveat that months of true growth attenuate it |
| Instructional-area scores (Table 7.8) | 0.87–0.88 mean | The domain sub-scores — MAP's own, on the operational pool |
Holding a pre-calibration simulation to the operational-pool number is a category error
The comparison to hold us to is 0.96 post-calibration, not pre.
